result: The authors used Cy3-dUTP labeling to mark newly synthesized DNA during S-phase, labeling chromatin domains ranging from 0.5 to 10 Mbp (with the majority at 0.5 Mbp), which they interpret as corresponding to topologically associated domains. The labeled structures were stable over cell cycles.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm the labeling method, noting 'This work is based on previous work published in 2015...in which the labeling method was demonstrated to be sound.' The technology and methods are described as 'solid' with no concerns raised about the labeling approach or DNA quantification.

result: The authors report that chromatin motion is constrained during S-phase compared to G1/G2 phases in both HeLa and IMR90 cells, with quantified diffusion rates showing significant decreases during S-phase. The effect was stronger in IMR90 cells, and chromatin exhibited anomalous subdiffusion.
evaluation: Reviewers identify this as a major conclusion, stating 'The authors report reduced chromatin mobility in S relative to G1 phase.' The revised manuscript 'included data from a diploid cell line IMR90...to strengthen the conclusions,' and reviewers note 'Overall, quality of the work is substantially improved,' indicating acceptance of these findings.

result: Chromatin in proximity to active replication sites (within 1 μm center-to-center distance) showed more restricted motion, with this effect vanishing at greater distances.
evaluation: Reviewers list 'Restricted chromatin motion occurred at sites in proximity to DNA replication sites' as one of the major conclusions without raising concerns. This finding is treated as an accepted result supporting the spatial relationship between replication and chromatin dynamics.

result: Upon aphidicolin treatment to inhibit DNA synthesis, the authors observed rapid inhibition of replication (99% of cells within 30 min), PCNA dissociation from chromatin, RPA accumulation, increased MCM2 phosphorylation (indicating helicase activation), and increased loading of DNA polymerase α while polymerases δ and ε showed minimal changes.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these biochemical observations. The description of aphidicolin effects and the molecular changes at replisomes are treated as established findings that support the main conclusions. No concerns are raised about the characterization of replisome component behavior.

result: The authors' key finding is that aphidicolin treatment, which inhibits DNA synthesis, paradoxically led to further restriction of chromatin motion in S-phase (beyond that seen during normal replication), while G1/G2 motion was unaffected. They conclude that replisome loading, not catalytic activity, restricts chromatin dynamics.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly identify 'Chromatin motion was restricted by the loading of replisomes, independent of DNA synthesis' as a major conclusion. This counterintuitive finding—that blocking synthesis increases constraint—is accepted without challenge and represents the central mechanistic insight of the paper.
